result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers offer well-matched tiers, cap AI search, and keep backup, trash and original downloads in every plan. B includes payment fees, gives price ranges to test, and says outright that it is not guessing rival prices, though it miscounts Family search cost as $1.80 instead of $0.90. A's math is mostly right but promises at least 35% margin and then shows 29–31% for Pro, and it states an unsupported 50–70% quota-usage figure and claims the free tier 'converts well'. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers set out similar tiers that cover each group's range, and both cap AI search. A's arithmetic has one error: it costs the Family plan's 300 searches at $1.80 when the correct figure is $0.90. That error overstates cost, so it is on the safe side. A keeps RAW and the plugin with Pro, frames its prices as ranges to test, and says outright that it has not guessed competitor prices. B puts RAW in Family. It also says worst-case margins are about 35% or better, which conflicts with its own 31% and 29% figures. And it asserts things it was not given: that usage is usually 50–70% of quota, and that the free tier 'converts well'.
